output.brief: The slowdown comes from one policy change, not from Corvane or the new hires. Credit Policy v14, effective 1 May, requires a full property appraisal for exposures above $150k. The old threshold was $500k. Property-secured loans now spend about 8 days in valuation, against 1.6 before. The valuation firm's turnaround hasn't changed: full appraisals took about 8.6 days before and after, and desktop valuations about 1.2. More loans now need the slower full appraisal. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, close to March's 5.6. Document collection at the branches with new hires matches the other branches. Consumer loans on Corvane are flat. Volume and Hub staffing don't explain it, because underwriting time is flat. I'm quite sure of this, with one caveat. The policy had an audit reason: desktop valuations came in a median 12% above full appraisals. The decision on that tradeoff belongs to the credit risk committee. Next steps: take the measured delay and the audit rationale to the committee. Don't withhold the Corvane payment, and don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. Check how many withdrawals come from the 30-day auto-close rule before spending money on win-back offers. I haven't established that slower approvals cause withdrawals.
